transcript.text: Every so often when I put the washing machine on the whole kitchen power goes off and I have to go to the fuse box and flick the switch back up. It doesn't happen every time. Indesit, IWE 7 something.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. This is an electrical safety issue. Because your washing machine is tripping the kitchen power (likely an RCD or earth-leakage breaker), there is a credible risk of electric shock. Please stop using the appliance until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The most common cause for this specific symptom in Indesit machines is the heater element developing an internal fault that allows electricity to 'leak' to earth (the metal casing). This usually happens once the cycle reaches the heating stage, but can sometimes occur earlier depending on the severity of the leak. Other possibilities include a faulty drain pump or damaged wiring inside the machine. To help narrow this down for when an engineer attends, could you tell me: does the power trip happen immediately when you switch it on (before any water enters), or only after a few minutes once the water has heated up?

It doesn't trip straight away. It's always a few minutes into a 40 or 60 degree wash, and it has never tripped on a cold wash, a quick 30 or a rinse and spin. I have been resetting it each time, so I'll stop now. There's been no burning smell and I haven't seen any sparking or scorching.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. The fact that it only trips a few minutes into a hot wash (40 or 60 degrees) and never on cold cycles suggests the fault is linked to the heating stage. This points strongly to the heater element developing an internal leak to earth (the metal casing). The water acts as a conductor, allowing current to escape when the element is live, which trips your RCD. Because this involves a live electrical fault in a wet appliance, it is not safe for you to repair or test further. Please do not attempt to open the machine or use a multimeter yourself. You need to have a qualified engineer check the heater element (and check the wiring) before using the machine again.

candidates: Heater element leaking to earth (short circuit) (high)
Drain pump or wiring harness fault (medium)
